title: INCOLOR SSR - Frameset Walkaround

takeaways.text: In January 2026 the retailer-linked presenter described each frameset as over US$3,000, with long waiting times because of demand.

Two painted customer frames with hardware and the integrated seat mast weighed just over 900 g (size 48) and just over 1,000 g (largest size shown). The maker's figure of about 780 g is a raw, unpainted mould weight; this premium paint was estimated at 130–150 g.
Repeats Incolor's claims of Silverstone wind-tunnel development and that its own test found the SSR faster than an S5 and an SL8; no independent data is shown.
Threaded T47A bottom bracket, UDH, flat-mount brakes and two rectangular-section aero bottles supplied with the frame.

A SRAM Red flat-mount rear caliper fitted the size 48 with a few millimetres to spare on a 140 mm rotor. For 160 mm, the presenter advises SRAM's own adapter, because taller third-party adapters may hit the seatstay.
Caliper measurements: the head tube front is about 34 mm wide and the seat mast about 15–15.5 mm.

The bayonet front end uses a standard OD1 steerer; brake hoses pass through a slot in the steerer, a bolt limits steering so the fork cannot hit the frame, and a cover hides cables entering Incolor's bar. Fitting a different bar is possible but not neat.

disclosure: China Cycling's founder also leads Panda Podium, a retailer that lists the Incolor SSR.
summary: Exact-model frameset walkaround retained as disclosed editorial context; current specifications, price and mainland purchase evidence come from the cited manufacturer and official-store records.
